memory.conflictsHint: These claims contradict each other. Pick the correct one or delete both.
memory.channelsHintHybrid: Both channels are live: paraphrase is matched by embeddings, exact identifiers by the lexical index.
memory.channelsHintDegraded: No memory in this workspace has an embedding yet, so the dense channel scores nothing and retrieval runs on keywords alone. Diversity re-ranking is inactive for the same reason.
memory.channelsHintNoEmbedder: No embedding model is wired, so queries can't be embedded either. Retrieval runs on keywords alone.
memory.breakerWhat: Circuit breaker: pauses memory retrieval after repeated failures so it can't stall every turn, then resumes on its own once things are stable.

memory.breakerDescOpen: Kept failing — recall is skipped for now
memory.tokenEstimateTitle: Estimate: the backend counts 1 token per wide character plus 1 per 4 other characters. Not a real tokenizer result, and deliberately on the high side. Tier budgets are enforced against this estimate.
memory.entryNewPlaceholder: A fact or preference the agent should remember (⌘/Ctrl + Enter to save)
memory.entryEmpty: No memories in this tier yet.
memory.entryReadOnly: Working memory is cleared every turn and can't be edited
memory.statusFilterTitle: Filter by lifecycle status. The default view lists active, pending and expired; archived and rejected have to be picked explicitly — but they must be reachable, or a mis-deleted memory is gone for good.
memory.confidenceTitle: How likely this is true, clamped to 5%–95%. Not the same thing as importance: a very important memory that is probably no longer true should not rank first.
memory.lastConfirmedTitle: When this was last confirmed to still hold. Freshness is measured from here, not from creation: a fact written three years ago and confirmed last week is more trustworthy than one written last month that nobody has mentioned since.

capabilitiesPage.title: Capabilities
capabilitiesPage.subtitle: Everything Ovolve can do is assembled here: plugins extend the app, skills inject domain knowledge, MCP connects external tools, subagents take on isolated work.

toolsPanel.desc: Every tool the agent can currently call — {{count}} in total, grouped by domain. Plugins and MCP servers ultimately add rows to this table.

modeMeaning.plan: Read-only, and the prompt asks it to write a plan then stop. Writes are refused outright — neither a granted permission nor a hook can rescue them.
modeMeaning.readonly: Read-only. Writes are refused, not asked. (Sub-agents only.)
modeMeaning.auto: Low risk runs; medium and high ask first. This is the default.

toolsPanel.criticalNote: One exception: critical calls ask in every mode, including full access, and are refused outright under plan. A single allow rule cannot silence critical either.
toolsPanel.baselineNote: Risk here is a BASELINE — the backend computes it with empty arguments. Real risk escalates with the arguments: git push is medium, but with --force it is critical.

plugins.desc: A plugin is a bundle: one directory plus a plugin.json, packaging skills and subagents behind a single name, version and on/off switch.

plugins.installHint: There is no marketplace, so installing means pointing at a path — same as skills. .agents/plugins and ~/.agents/plugins are scanned at startup.
plugins.emptyHint: Paste a plugin directory path above to install one. A plugin can carry skills (SKILL.md) and subagents (YAML); one install brings them all in.
plugins.unsupported: Manifest keys not supported yet, ignored: {{keys}}

mcp.desc: MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers mount external tools into the agent's tool table. The config format is the same one common MCP clients use.

subagents.desc: A subagent runs in its own context. The main agent delegates through the task tool and gets back only the conclusion, keeping the intermediate work out of the main window.
subagents.emptyHint: Built-ins come from app/backend/subagent_registry.py. Drop a YAML file into app/backend/subagents/ to add one or override a built-in by name.

settingsPage.notifyTitle: Notify me when a task finishes
settingsPage.notifyDesc: Shows a native OS toast when the agent settles a turn; clicking it jumps straight to that session
settingsPage.notifyAria: Notify me when a task finishes
settingsPage.notifyWhenFocusedDesc: By default you're only pinged when the window is away or another session is open. Turn this on to always get the toast.
settingsPage.notifyFailuresOnlyDesc: Stays quiet on success and only interrupts you when something breaks
settingsPage.notifyTestDesc: Fires a sample toast right now so you can confirm the OS isn't muting or blocking it
settingsPage.notifyBlocked: The OS is blocking notifications for this app. Re-allow it under Windows Settings → System → Notifications.
settingsPage.closeToTrayTitle: Minimize to the system tray on close
settingsPage.closeToTrayDesc: Clicking X only hides the window — background turns, schedules and bots keep running, and the tray icon brings it back. Turn this off to make X quit the app and terminate everything in flight.
settingsPage.closeToTrayAria: Minimize to system tray on close
settingsPage.trayHint: Right-click the tray icon for: show / hide window, new chat, settings, quit
settingsPage.behaviorDesc: Tune the per-turn tool-loop ceiling and the context-fold cadence. Applies to the next turn immediately after saving — no restart.
settingsPage.maxStepsHint: Hard ceiling on tool-calling rounds within one user turn, so a confused model cannot loop forever and burn the budget. The soft-landing notice fires two steps before the cap so the model can write its handover.
settingsPage.foldThresholdHint: When context usage crosses this share, older turns are folded into a summary before the next turn starts.
settingsPage.foldEmergencyHint: Forces a fold immediately at this share instead of waiting for a turn boundary. Never lower than the auto threshold.
settingsPage.foldCooldownHint: Minimum gap between two folds, so back-to-back compaction cannot burn tokens for nothing.
settingsPage.fallbackModelDesc: When the primary model is unavailable or over context, the backend tries this one. Leave empty to use any other enabled model from the registry.
settingsPage.gitTrustDesc: Require explicit trust before write operations on repos not in the trust list. The list lives at ~/.ovolve/trusted_repos.txt and is plain text you can audit.

sandboxStatus.fullDesc: Commands run inside the OS sandbox; file access is limited by the {{policy}}.
sandboxStatus.partialDesc: Basic isolation is active; some limits still rely on the {{policy}}.
sandboxStatus.offDesc: Only the {{policy}} applies — no kernel-level fallback.
sandboxStatus.policyFileHint: Power users can place sandbox-policy.yaml in the workspace or home directory (see app/sandbox-policy.example.yaml).

settingsPage.privacyDesc: Data retention and telemetry preferences. Changes apply instantly.
settingsPage.telemetryDesc: Records call spans and performance data to a local log for diagnostics. Turning it off stops collection immediately; nothing is ever uploaded.
settingsPage.autoConfirmDesc: When on, the confirm-every-step mode still auto-approves read-only low-risk tools and only asks for medium/high risk. When off, that mode asks for every single call. Irreversible operations ignore this switch and always ask.
settingsPage.rulesDesc: Calls matching a rule skip the per-call confirmation. Answering "always allow" during a turn leaves one here. Irreversible operations (force push, hard reset…) always ask — rules do not apply to them.
settingsPage.streamTimeoutHint: Wall-clock ceiling for one streamed model request. Raise it for slow reasoning models or weak networks so long thinking is not cut off.
settingsPage.hooks.desc: Extend agent behaviour with lifecycle hooks — inject context, deny tool calls, or react to events. Configured via hooks.json.
settingsPage.hooks.noConfig: No hooks.json found — add one to register hooks.
settingsPage.hooks.empty: No hooks registered. Add a hooks.json to extend agent behaviour.
settingsPage.hooks.configDesc: Hooks are defined in hooks.json at the project root or ~/.agents/hooks.json. Each hook is a shell/process command: exit 0 passes, exit 2 denies the action, anything else is an error. Hooks can inject additional context or override permission decisions.
settingsPage.contextSectionDesc: How memory is retrieved and injected into context — plus the agent's factual beliefs about this workspace and the only place to arbitrate when two contradict.
settingsPage.overviewDesc: What's currently in effect across all approval families (read-only). Edit each family in its own group above.
settingsPage.overviewLoadFailed: Overview failed to load — each family's own settings above still work.
settingsPage.outboundProxyDesc: Tool-internal web search and page fetching go through this proxy (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:7890). Leave empty to follow system/env proxy settings.
settingsPage.outboundTavilyDesc: Optional. When set, web search uses the Tavily API (structured results, no HTML scraping); otherwise DuckDuckGo. The key is stored encrypted on this machine.
settingsPage.outboundTavilyConfigured: Configured ({{masked}}). Enter a new value to replace it, or click Clear key to remove.
